summary:
Jigawa State stands under Nigeria's national framework and its own Sharia Penal Code Law 2000 (Law No. 12 of 2000), signed 18 December 2000 and in operation from 27 December 2000 (Jigawa State Gazette Vol. 1 No. 12). Jigawa is one of twelve northern states that had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation by 2002, and, with those states, remains among the only states where Sharia courts hold jurisdiction to try criminal cases.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on Nigeria (June 2025) lists Jigawa in a twelve-state Sharia penalties table under a Sharia Penal Code (2000). Married men face death by stoning; unmarried men face 100 lashes and imprisonment of up to one year; same-sex acts between women carry up to 50 lashes with imprisonment of up to six months. The June 2025 note confirms the Sharia penal layer remains the operative criminal frame for Muslims in Jigawa.

Jigawa's code sits among four states, with Gombe, Kano and Zamfara, whose sodomy offence punishes unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajam); lesbianism carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment. Jigawa's code includes an 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' explanation of the offence and criminalises conduct the federal code does not reach, including women's same-sex conduct.
tangentialFactors:
Zamfara's governor was the first to extend Sharia to criminal law, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000; by 2002 the model had spread to eleven further states including Jigawa.

The UK Home Office note's section 8.2.20 covers the Sharia codes in force in Kano, Borno, Kaduna and other northern states, placing Jigawa's regime within a wider regional pattern rather than an isolated state code.
localsOnly:
Jigawa's Sharia Penal Code Law 2000 applies as the operative criminal frame for Muslims in the state, with Sharia courts holding jurisdiction over criminal cases; the code reaches women's same-sex conduct, which the federal code does not.

For Muslim residents, exposure under the state code is graded by marital status: married men convicted of sodomy face stoning to death, while unmarried men face 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment. Women convicted of lesbianism face up to 50 lashes and up to six months' imprisonment.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Jigawa-specific enforcement incidents, arrests, prosecutions or sentences under the state Sharia code are documented in this inventory; the inventory supplies the statute's text and penalties, not evidence of how Jigawa courts have applied them.

Whether Jigawa's code has been applied against transgender residents specifically, as distinct from its same-sex conduct provisions, is not sourced here.

Interaction between the state Sharia layer and the national SSMPA in Jigawa, including which authority would charge a given case, is unresolved in the sources provided.
